question: Which independently proposed agent-ee enhancements should become bounded implementation tickets, preserving evidence authority and single-writer review isolation?
scope: agent-ee enhancement roadmap and detailed Plane backlog designs

authority_boundary.authority_source: Explicit thread goal: independently run ADHD, discuss, gain consensus and publish detailed Plane work items.
authorized_scope: Detailed backlog designs and Plane publication

evidence.summary: Owner authorizes independent ideation, design discussion, consensus priority and Plane publication; feature execution is not requested.

Scope/2 evidence gates, independent contexts, one repair writer, conservative convergence and documented qualification limits define the preservation boundary. Docs task found RC step default and standalone external-profile gaps; no automatic campaign resume exists. Tests cover baseline/margins/locks/empirical epochs; historical live adjudication fails closed.

evidence.summary: Draft roadmap states ranked proposals, alternatives including no change, exact preservation/authority boundaries, per-item acceptance tests, versioning and explicit failure cases. This proves the content of the proposed plan, not implementation efficacy or final consensus. Publication can be revised through issue updates and a docs commit; no feature code is changed.
satisfies: alternatives including no change where viable

evidence.summary: Actual KiCad geometry execution on a disposable board reports pass for five straight segments despite an added 0.05 mm PCB_ARC and declared 0.20 mm straight-segment criterion. Observation supports explicit coverage extension; it does not establish ERC/DRC failure, physical validation or a completed adversarial review.

assertions.text: Owner requested a planning and publication deliverable; implementation and hardware release were not requested.
Native arc reproduction demonstrates the current straight-segment coverage limit; extending the criterion requires explicit semantics and verification.

Prefer explicit failure/capability/applicability contracts and bounded qualified extensions while retaining existing independent-review and sealed-check authority. Publish only after explicit three-party consensus.
alternatives: No feature change; retain current documented limits
tradeoffs: Bounded contracts offer less coverage than general solvers but make unsupported domains explicit.
Qualification and compatibility gates add engineering work.
Scores and team consensus do not prove physical efficacy.

assertions.text: Parent, Fable and Argon explicitly agreed to final proposal order 1,3,4,5,6,13,7,8,9,10,11,12 and the retained detailed contracts. The coordinator published and read back the roadmap parent and twelve child designs.
assertions.owner: repository owner, via explicitly requested team consensus
assertions.authority: User thread goal authorizes team selection and Plane publication; final confirmations retained in fable-consensus.md and argon-consensus.md.

General physical solving and automatic inverse model fitting

Explicit final order and contract agreement from parent, Fable and Argon
